chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from Hannan ibn Sadeyr, from his father who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'Can the son suffice [in repaying the debt of duty] to his father?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no sufficing for him except in two characteristics: if the father is an owned slave, so his son buys him and frees him, or if there are debts upon him, so he (the son) fulfils them on his behalf.'
ai.seo_question: How can a son repay his father according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that while parental gratitude is paramount, specific financial redemption is limited to two distinct scenarios: manumission if the father is enslaved, or debt settlement if he is indebted. This hadith is often cited by Shia jurists to distinguish between general *birr* (righteousness) and specific financial obligations, highlighting the practical dimensions of filial piety in classical Islamic society. It underscores the son's role as a provider who can alleviate the father's worldly burdens, thereby serving as a tangible form of repayment for their upbringing.
